source_period: 2013-05 A-series survey exterior, not B restoration
findings: Seven overview/elevation/top views contain the complete model; top view support margin is tight but not clipped. Two details intentionally crop the building.
Five-sided chamfer is present, with entrance projection not flattened into the two street elevations.
East annex is two-storey south and one-storey north, sloping outwards; three surviving upper north east windows remain visible.
Roof is flat without invented full perimeter parapet. Diagonal raised sign crest and north-high stair shed profile are distinct.
Two circular roof pads are low RC-base proxies, not invented tanks. Other rectangular pads are explicitly omitted in README.
Closed roller shutter, opaque noticeboards covering original diamond-window positions, and west blocked former doorway match the stated survey scope.
Main rectangular/round/semicircular opening rhythms inspected against source204/205; frames and panes remain simplified opaque proxies.
Neutral badge disc is now visible and is not represented as a clock or legible historical emblem.
README explicitly discloses approximate scales, omitted equipment, unknown base heights, solid exterior mass, blind roof door, and no physical trial print.
V3 six crest short horizontal accents are visible as three per side in front/north/west views. Independent outer-normal test confirms all six project beyond crest face rather than being embedded.
limitations: This is not a photorealistic damage reconstruction or complete interior survey.
Graphical dimensions approximately ±3%; fine opening grids, cornice profiles, shutter ribs, colours and cladding pitch simplified.
Independent visual/geometry approval does not certify printing success, structural safety or publication state.
reinspection: V3 front inspected at full resolution and all nine normalized views in contact sheet; prior v2 detail inspection supplemented, v2 approval superseded.
